chunks: From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn Bukhtari and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That he prayed two rak'at in the Mosque of the Tree, and concluded the Ihram, then went out, and was brought a dish of khabis containing saffron, and he ate from it.

key_terms.خَبِيصٍ: A type of food, often a porridge or stew
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ الشَّجَرَةِ: The Mosque of the Tree, a significant location in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam eat after concluding his Ihram in the Mosque of the Tree?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfahani highlights the practical application of Ihram regulations, specifically illustrating that the Imam (peace be upon him) concluded his ritual consecration after performing two units of prayer in the Mosque of the Tree. The subsequent consumption of saffron-infused khabis serves as a clear precedent for the permissibility of eating scented or mixed foods once the state of Ihram has been formally ended, reinforcing the juristic distinction between the state of consecration and ordinary life.
